note: Revision Manager prunes old revisions of any revisionable content entity type via RevisionManager plugins: 'amount' (settings.amount = keep newest N) and 'age' (settings.age = delete older than N months). Global config lives in revision_manager.settings: enabled_entities (map entity_type=>bool), defaults (entity_type=>plugin_id=>{id,status,settings}), disable_automatic_queueing, verbose_log. Bundle overrides are third-party settings on the bundle config entity, e.g. node.type.article -> third_party_settings.revision_manager.amount = {id,status,settings:{amount:N}}. Both plugins enabled => conservative (delete only if all agree); current + forward revisions always kept. Cleanup is queue-based (remove_revisions queue); Drush 'rm:queue' enqueues all enabled entities. Permission administer revision_manager; settings route revision_manager.settings at /admin/config/content/revision-manager. Shipped install defaults: enabled_entities {}, defaults {}, disable_automatic_queueing false, verbose_log false. medium cases read back configured Amount count / enabled entity types; hard cases write a global Amount default and a per-bundle override, verified against live config.

evals.prompt: What two revision-retention strategies (plugins) does the Drupal revision_manager module ship, and what does each one do?
evals.expected_output: It ships the 'amount' plugin (keep a minimum number of the newest revisions, settings.amount) and the 'age' plugin (delete revisions older than a chosen number of months, settings.age). Both always preserve the current and forward revisions.

evals.prompt: Which Drush command does revision_manager provide to schedule revision cleanup, and what does it actually do?
evals.expected_output: drush rm:queue batch-enqueues all enabled entities (respecting each type/bundle's enabled plugins) into the remove_revisions queue; the actual deletions happen when that queue is processed (e.g. by cron).

evals.prompt: If I enable BOTH the Amount and Age criteria in revision_manager for a content type, how does it decide which revisions get deleted?
evals.expected_output: Deletion becomes conservative: a revision is deleted only if EVERY enabled plugin independently flags it (the intersection of Amount's and Age's decisions). The more criteria you enable, the fewer revisions are removed; current and forward revisions are never deleted.

evals.prompt: On this site, revision management is enabled for nodes with the Amount plugin. Inspect the live revision_manager configuration and state the minimum number of revisions it is set to keep for nodes.
evals.expected_output: It keeps 7 revisions: revision_manager.settings -> defaults.node.amount.settings.amount = 7 (with amount.status true and enabled_entities.node true).

evals.prompt: Inspect the live revision_manager configuration on this site and list which entity types currently have revision management enabled.
evals.expected_output: Node and taxonomy_term are enabled: revision_manager.settings -> enabled_entities has node: true and taxonomy_term: true.

evals.prompt: Using the revision_manager module, enable revision management for the node entity type and set its default Amount policy to keep a minimum of 3 revisions. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: revision_manager.settings has enabled_entities.node = true and defaults.node.amount = {id: amount, status: true, settings: {amount: 3}}.

evals.prompt: Revision management is enabled for nodes on this site. Override the policy for the Article content type specifically so that Articles keep a minimum of 10 revisions (Amount plugin), stored as a bundle-level override. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The node.type.article config entity gains a third-party setting revision_manager.amount with settings.amount = 10 (status true), overriding the entity-type default for Articles.
